articles.title_orig: Nissan's Chinese Truck Goes On Sale In Mexico And Other Markets
articles.title_zh: Nissan's Chinese Truck Goes On Sale In Mexico And Other Markets
articles.content_orig:
As it turns out, the Frontier Pro is no longer a China-only curiosity. Originally unveiled at Auto Shanghai in April 2025, the electrified pickup is now going (kinda) global, although Nissan is giving it a different name in some markets. Also known as the Navara Pro, the midsize truck designed and built in China heads to export markets in many parts of the world.
Mexico will be the first market outside China to pick up the workhorse, with sales kicking off this month. It starts at 899,900 pesos, which works out to around $50,000 at current exchange rates. It combines a 1.5-liter gas engine with an electric motor for a total system output of 350 horsepower and 447 pound-feet (660 Newton-meters) of torque. Between the gas tank and the 20-kWh battery pack, it has a driving range of 600 miles (966 kilometers), with 47 miles (75 kilometers) covered in electric mode.
The Philippines, Middle East, and other Latin American markets will follow before the end of the year, while Australia and New Zealand are scheduled to join the party in 2027 as the first right-hand-drive markets.
2026 Nissan Frontier Pro (China)
Despite the familiar name, the Frontier Pro has practically nothing in common with the truck sold in the U.S. The Chinese-market pickup is based on the Nissan Dongfeng Z9 and measures 217.3 inches (5,520 millimeters) long with an 130-inch (3,300-mm) wheelbase.
The biggest talking point remains the plug-in hybrid powertrain. In its original Chinese specification, a turbocharged 1.5-liter four-cylinder works with an electric motor integrated into the transmission to produce more than 402 horsepower and 590 pound-feet (800 Newton-meters) of torque. Nissan quoted an electric-only range of up to 84 miles (135 kilometers) on China's CLTC cycle.
Those figures make the Frontier Pro a particularly interesting proposition in a segment increasingly invaded by electrified pickups. It also comes with intelligent all-wheel drive, selectable 4High and 4Low modes, an available electromechanical rear differential lock, and dedicated Hybrid, Pure Electric, Performance, and Snow modes.
And because this is a pickup, Nissan hasn't forgotten about the useful stuff. The PHEV gets vehicle-to-load capability, allowing the truck to supply electricity to external equipment. The Chinese version can deliver up to 6 kW through its V2L setup.
2026 Nissan Frontier Pro (China)
Nissan isn't putting all its eggs in the PHEV basket. The global Frontier Pro/Navara Pro has been engineered around multiple powertrains, including 1.5- and 2.0-liter plug-in hybrid setups as well as internal-combustion engines. Exact configurations will depend on the market.
Interestingly, Nissan says the ICE version will be offered in the Middle East, while the PHEV will be available in Latin America, ASEAN, and Oceania. That makes the Frontier Pro more than simply an electrified pickup exported from China; it's becoming part of Nissan's broader global product strategy.
There's also an important production footnote here. The Frontier Pro/Navara Pro is the first Nissan model developed and manufactured in China specifically for global export. It's built by Zhengzhou Nissan, Nissan's Chinese joint venture, as the company increasingly treats China as an engineering and manufacturing hub rather than simply another sales market.
2026 Nissan Frontier Pro (China)
Nissan says the strategy will allow it to combine the speed and competitiveness of Chinese development with its own engineering and quality standards. The company is using a similar approach for other products, including plans to export the N7 electric sedan from China to markets in ASEAN and Latin America.
For American truck buyers, there isn't much to get excited about yet. The Frontier Pro isn't replacing the familiar D41 Frontier, and Nissan hasn't announced plans to bring this China-built pickup to the United States, where it would immediately be slapped with the 25-percent Chicken Tax and tariffs.
For everyone else, however, things are getting considerably more interesting. Nissan is taking a truck that originally looked like an intriguing China-market experiment and turning it into a global product as it tries to bounce back after many challenging years.
As the saying goes, if you can't beat them, join them. Nissan isn't the only one doing this sort of thing as other legacy automakers are also deepening their ties with China to export vehicles internationally.

articles.title_orig: America shut out Chinese EVs. Britain welcomed them — and now faces a difficult choice
articles.title_zh: America shut out Chinese EVs. Britain welcomed them — and now faces a difficult choice
articles.content_orig:
The U.K. broke with the U.S. by opening its doors to China's electric vehicle juggernaut .
Chinese EVs face only a 10% standard import duty in Britain, one of the largest major overseas markets without additional China-specific tariffs. Japan and Norway also lack them.
It's in contrast to the U.S., where a 100% tariff effectively shut Chinese EVs out. The European Union , the U.K.'s biggest trading partner, has manufacturer-specific duties on Chinese EVs of up to 35.3%, in addition to a standard 10% import duty on all foreign cars.
Now, the U.K. faces a difficult choice, as EU proposals may force it to impose tariffs to match the bloc's.
At the weekend, The Sunday Times reported that U.K. Business Minister Jonathan Reynolds is considering matching the EU's levy on Chinese EVs to avoid the pain of so-called " Made in Europe " proposals, which could hurt domestic companies selling into the EU.
A U.K. government spokesperson reiterated to CNBC that it had not imposed tariffs on Chinese EVs but added: "We continue to engage closely with industry so that our approach reflects the sector's and UK's national interests."
The Made in Europe legislation, part of the EU's Industrial Accelerator Act , is designed to protect the bloc's industries from unfair international competition by prioritizing European-made goods.
An EU official told the Financial Times in September that London would need to raise tariffs on Chinese EVs and align more closely with EU trade policy to avoid "Made in Europe" barriers.
The decision is finely balanced, given Prime Minister Andy Burnham's desire to reset relations with the EU , which the U.K. formally left in 2020, and the likelihood of China responding with retaliatory measures.
A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in London said it had expressed "serious concern" to Britain about the reports about potential tariffs.
"China is firmly opposed to any discriminatory practice involving tariff hikes or restrictive measures on Chinese products," a spokesperson said Tuesday. "We will continue to follow developments and respond accordingly," they said.
Chinese car brands have swiftly captured market share in the U.K.
Analysis by JATO Dynamics found that registrations of Chinese automakers, or original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), across both battery-electric and hybrid powertrains, rose to 519,424 between the start of January and the end of August, lifting their total market share to 28.1%. That's up sharply from 12.9% in the same period in 2025.
Hybrids accounted for the larger increase, adding 62,655 registrations versus 32,565 for battery-electric vehicles.
"That matters for policy," Paul Hilton, head of retail at JATO Dynamics, told CNBC by email.
"Tariffs aimed only at Chinese-built battery EVs could slow one part of the expansion, but would not address hybrid growth, vehicles made outside China or the underlying advantages in cost, product cadence and supply chains," Hilton said.
"A durable UK response should pair any evidence-based trade remedy with incentives for local production, competitive energy and battery costs, charging infrastructure, skills and alignment with European market-access rules."
The bestselling car in the U.K. last month was not a Tesla or a Ford — but the Jaecoo 7 from China.
The mid-size SUV, nicknamed the “Temu Range Rover,” starts at about £29,000 ($38,350) in the U.K., compared with roughly £45,500 for a Land Rover Discovery Sport.
The Jaecoo 7's nationwide sales climbed to 10,814 in September, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders, outpacing the Tesla Model 3, Ford Puma and Kia Sportage.
Rico Luman, senior sector economist for transport and logistics at ING, said the growing policy gap between Britain and the EU is leaving the U.K. with limited options, besides tariffs, if it wants to maintain a level playing field with the bloc.
Speaking to CNBC by email, Luman said exclusion from the Made in Europe initiative could have “significant consequences” for existing businesses, making closer alignment with EU trade policy increasingly difficult to avoid.
"It's generally quite remarkable that batteries from China are exempted from EU tariffs," Luman said.
"At the same time this is logical as production in Europe isn't up to speed and Europe lacks the rare earth minerals and refinery capacity behind it," he added.

It will mark the first official visit to China since 2018 for Steinmeier, a former foreign minister whose decade-long tenure as president ends in March 2027. The visit will coincide with Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s trips to Japan and South Korea before the end of October.
Germany’s president is the head of state, while political power sits primarily with the chancellor and government, making Steinmeier’s a largely ceremonial role. The president does, however, represent Germany abroad.

articles.title_orig: Šefčovič goes to Beijing with a final plea to avoid an EU-China trade war
articles.title_zh: Šefčovič goes to Beijing with a final plea to avoid an EU-China trade war
articles.content_orig:
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney and U.S. President Donald Trump in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, on Oct. 13, 2025.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s “ Canada Strong ” strategy vows to “unite” and “secure” the nation in the face of an ongoing trade war with the U.S. Canadians are encouraged to support his efforts to “stand up to” President Donald Trump and help “build a stronger Canada.”
But Carney’s united front is being tested once more, following separatist Parti Québécois’ (PQ) win in Quebec’s provincial election on Monday. The win came just two weeks before Alberta is set to vote on Oct. 19 over whether to remain in Canada or move ahead with a second binding vote on separation. The PQ has already pledged its intention to hold a referendum on Quebec independence. “The courageous battle of Francophones to protect their language and culture will succeed when they have their own country,” said Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, Quebec’s incoming Premier, during his victory speech.
However, Plamondon has vowed that no such referendum will be held “as long as Trump is President of the United States,” citing the political upheaval of the trade standoff.
Even if he were to change his mind, holding a referendum without a majority in Quebec’s National Assembly would prove difficult, experts say. The party fell five seats short of the 64 needed to form a majority government. “In order to have a referendum, you need to have the question adopted by the National Assembly of Quebec, and Plamondon is not going to have the votes for that,” says Stéphane Paquin, a professor of public policy and international political economy at the École nationale d’administration publique (ENAP) in Montreal.
Still, the mere threat of a separatist agenda undoubtedly challenges Carney’s efforts to maintain a cohesive approach at a time when Canada needs to put its strongest foot forward. Carney congratulated Plamondon on his victory by stressing that “building a stronger Quebec is at the heart of our mission to build a stronger Canada.”
After trade negotiations between the U.S. and Canada collapsed in August, Carney met virtually with provincial and territorial Premiers to strategize. He used the opportunity to underscore his view that “Canada is strongest when governments stand together.” The trade standoff with the U.S. comes after months of escalating tensions, as Trump has repeatedly threatened to annex Canada and make it the “51st state” since returning to office.
Despite PQ’s victory, there are few outward signs that the majority French-speaking province is seeking independence. Polling by 338Canada found that around 70% of Quebecers opposed independence as recently as Oct. 4. In a Pallas Data-L’Actualité-Qc125 poll published on Sept. 15, 64% of Quebecers said they were against holding a third referendum on sovereignty—suggesting the unsuccessful attempts in 1980 and 1995 did little to whet Quebecers’ appetite
Nor should the separatist party's victory necessarily be interpreted as a rejection of Carney. The Prime Minister remains popular in Quebec—a poll by Abacus Data in late September found Carney had a net impression of +46, with 59% of Quebecers identifying Trump and his Administration as one of the three most important issues facing Canada.
Quebec has been particularly vulnerable to tariffs imposed by the Trump Administration.
An August analysis by the National Bank of Canada estimates that Quebec faces the highest average effective U.S. tariff rate in Canada at roughly 11%. According to provincial data , Quebec’s exports of metal ores and non-metallic minerals dropped by nearly 25% in 2025, alongside double-digit declines in autos, chemicals, and plastics products.
André Lecours, a professor of political studies at the University of Ottawa, says the presence of Trump was felt heavily throughout the Quebec election, as his trade threats had already dampened the separatist movement.
“It prompted PQ to commit to holding a referendum only after the departure of the President,” Lecours says. “Most Quebecers don't want an independence referendum at this point, anyway, so it helped to make the referendum something distant.”
Lecours says it is “not in the DNA of PQ to collaborate with the government of Canada” and suggests there may be difficult conversations ahead.
That tension is already visible over the trade war, he notes. When Carney decided to match U.S. tariffs “dollar-for-dollar” , Plamondon publicly opposed the approach, saying “it directly harms” Quebec's economy.
“The intergovernmental relations with Quebec is going to be a challenge, especially in the context of the negotiations with the U.S.,” Lecours predicts. “If there's anything in these negotiations driving towards an agreement that seems to diminish Quebec, its economy, or its sectors, then PQ is going to denounce it.”
“PQ still wants to have a referendum on independence, so it has very few incentives to make this relationship [with Carney] work or seem productive,” Lecours adds.
The PQ has also voiced opposition to the federal government's proposed high-speed rail project that would connect Toronto to Montreal and on to Quebec City, which could cause further issues.
Leader of the Parti Quebecois (PQ) Paul St-Pierre Plamondon makes a speech in Quebec, Canada, on Oct. 5, 2026. Andrej Ivanov––Getty Images
Carney is facing a separatist challenge in the energy-rich province of Alberta. An Oct. 19 referendum, set to also include immigration and constitutional questions, will ask Albertans: “Should Alberta remain a province of Canada, or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada?”
The vote will not itself be a binding referendum on separation. Instead, it will determine whether the government should begin the legal process required to hold such a referendum.
Polling from 338Canada on Sept. 20 showed 74% of Albertans wish to remain in Canada.
Carney’s government has meanwhile sought to court support in Alberta through new business proposals, including a high-speed rail line that would connect Calgary to Edmonton via Red Deer, linking Alberta's two largest cities, and the Pacific Link oil pipeline project, which would carry crude oil from Bruderheim, Alberta, to a deep-water port near Delta, British Columbia.
“That’s the scale of what Alberta and Canada can achieve—and the speed with which we can achieve it–when we work together,” Carney said on Oct. 1, announcing that Canada will fast-track the approval process for the pipeline. “And we will build together—with Alberta, British Columbia, and every province and territory—in the true spirit of cooperative federalism, harnessing the full force of a united Canada.”
But experts say Carney must strike a careful balance, with efforts to address separatist discontent in Alberta potentially influencing perceptions elsewhere, particularly in Quebec.
“In order to prevent support for independence in Alberta, the Carney government’s strategy is to put more money and investment in the direction of Alberta,” says Paquin. “[Quebecans] might compare what he's doing to Alberta to what he does to Quebec. If he has a stronger stance against Quebec or a more aggressive approach, then it could lead to more support for Quebec independence.”

articles.title_zh: Why China’s new air force base in Laos could rattle Vietnam

Hanoi likely to view the Ban Keun facility as Beijing’s bid to ‘encroach into its area of influence’ in Vientiane, analysts say
China’s National Defence Ministry said last Tuesday that the joint support and training facility at Ban Keun Airport in the Laotian capital would strengthen the expertise of local air force pilots and was “not directed against any third party”.
“The establishment and operation of the two institutions reflect mutual respect and equal consultation between China and Laos, aligning with domestic laws of both countries, as well as international law and common practices,” the ministry said in a statement.
It added that the installation, widely described as China’s third overseas defence base, “contributes to enhancing practical military cooperation, as well as promoting regional peace and stability”.

articles.title_orig: Christa Pike’s Lawyers Say She Is Angry and Confused After Failed Execution
articles.title_zh: Christa Pike’s Lawyers Say She Is Angry and Confused After Failed Execution
articles.content_orig:
A judge sided with the Tennessee inmate and ruled that evidence from her botched execution should be preserved.
• Christa Pike’s attorneys said they believed she was “brain-dead” after her botched execution last week – before she woke up and started talking. She is “ angry and confused about everything right now,” but is “very aware that the state tried to execute her,” attorney Randy Spivey told reporters. Pike has a “long road to recovery,” he added.
• The attorneys spoke after they were granted an emergency motion ordering the state to preserve evidence related to the execution. This includes 911 calls and communications between any state officials as well as physical evidence, Judge I’Ashea Myles said.
• Pike, who was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, was to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in 200 years.
Our live coverage has ended. Scroll down for updates on today’s court hearing and the latest from Christa Pike’s attorneys following her botched execution.
A judge ruled today the state of Tennessee must preserve all evidence related to Christa Pike’s failed execution.
This includes 911 calls and communications between any state officials as well as physical evidence, Judge I’Ashea Myles said, after hearing arguments.
Pike is conscious and speaking, her attorneys said, despite it appearing the night before that she was brain-dead and would be taken off life support. She was hospitalized after surviving two ostensibly lethal doses of pentobarbital last week.
Lauren del Valle, Maureen Chowdhury, August Phillips and Rebekah Riess contributed reporting.
Lawyers for a Texas man are asking a judge to pause his execution , citing the failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee last week.
Jamaal Howard is set to be executed by lethal injection later today , the first since Pike. Howard, 46, was found guilty of capital murder in the 2000 killing of Vickie Swartout, 42, who was shot once in the chest during a robbery.
In the filing, the attorneys requested more information about the lethal dose of pentobarbital the Texas Department of Criminal Justice planned to use, the AP reported.
Pike’s lawyers allege that issues with IV lines allowed the barbiturate to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream .
There is another execution scheduled in Florida next week, a state that has carried out the most executions so far this year, according to the Death Penalty Information Center . All of them used lethal injection, data shows.
Michelle Nowell, a Tennessee resident, said the state has “paid enough” for Christa Pike, citing the state’s rising bill from the continuation of her case after her botched execution last week.
“We have paid for Christa Pike, and now we’re paying for attorneys, and now we’re paying for hospital bills, and now they’re talking about lawsuits,” Nowell told CNN. “And the worst part is that Colleen has been forgotten.”
Pike was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death for the brutal 1995 killing of Colleen Slemmer, a fellow student at a job training facility.
Nowell pushed back on Pike’s attorneys statement describing her botched execution as “cruel and unusual” and to those who say Pike has “changed” in her more than 30 years in prison.
“Colleen is the one that knew cruel and unusual punishment,” she said.
Nowell said the state handled Pike’s execution “absolutely terribly.”
“I think it’s shameful,” Nowell said. “I’m a Tennessean, born and raised, a voter, and I know that our governor is going to be leaving soon, in January, and my hope is that Gov. (Bill) Lee will do the right thing and follow through with this execution.”
Jerri Green, Tennessee’s Democratic candidate for governor, who is running against Republican US Sen. Marsha Blackburn, has vowed to “enact a moratorium on all future executions,” in the state.
“True respect for the victims and their families means a justice system built on honesty, fairness, and safety, not cruelty, endless systemic failure, and secrecy. The facts are clear: the death penalty has proven to be an ineffective deterrent to violent crime, it is vastly more expensive than life imprisonment, and it is riddled with bias,” her statement reads in part.
“While the rest of the world reels from a botched execution that went horribly wrong, Blackburn is doubling down, calling to bring back the electric chair. That is barbaric, and it has no place in our state,” Green said of her opponent.
“As a public defender who has seen the devastating flaws in our justice system firsthand, my stance remains unshakeable: true pro-life values mean rejecting the death penalty entirely, and as Governor, I will enact a moratorium on all future executions,” she added.
Christa Pike’s attorney requested that her hand be unshackled as she receives medical care at a hospital after her botched execution.
Myles asked Ihnen had an affidavit from the medical personnel stating this request, and the attorney said he didn’t, but could provide it. The judge said she would make a decision after the document is submitted.
The state interjected on the request and pointed to Pike’s “escape history.” The judge said the request only includes unshackling Pike’s hand, not feet, and that she is reserving her judgment on this matter until she hears from the medical personnel.
Christa Pike’s attorney said he noticed “extraordinary” swelling of her hands following her botched execution attempt.
“Her hands looked like if you were to blow up a surgical glove,” he said. “The swelling was extraordinary, and that’s, that’s probably as far as I can go.”
Earlier, in court, her attorneys requested that Pike’s hand be unshackled while she is in the hospital due to the “extensive damage done to her arms and hands.”
Attorneys for Christa Pike thought she was brain-dead Monday and would be taken off life support the following day, but “to the shock of everyone,” on Tuesday, she woke up and began to talk, attorney Randy Spivey with the Tennessee Office of the Post-Conviction Defender said.
“I do not have an explanation for what happened between Monday night and Tuesday morning, but what we do know is that Christa has a long road to recovery,” Spivey said.
Pike has pneumonia and a blood clot in one of her arms, and she is not able to swallow yet and is therefore not eating, according to Spivey.
“She cannot move either of her arms. Both of her arms and hands are tremendously swollen, and we do not know what, if any, function she will regain in her arms. But we do know that there’s a long road ahead,” he added.
The botched execution of Christa Pike was “foreseeable and foreseen,” one of her lawyers, Randy Spivey, reiterated today after a court hearing to preserve evidence after the incident.
“What happened to Christa is exactly what the state was warned would happen, and there are so many questions that need to be answered, not by Christa — but by the state of Tennessee,” he said at a news conference outside the courthouse.
Her lawyer said Pike was “at peace” in the moments before her execution. She was “kind and polite” as officials struggled to set the IV lines for more than an hour, Spivey said.
“And then she woke up in a hospital surrounded by people she didn’t know with a tube down her throat. We don’t know the toll all of this will take, but Christa is a survivor, and we remain hopeful,” Spivey said.
Pike’s attorneys previously said they had warned courts beforehand that Pike’s vein issues would make it difficult to carry out the lethal injection.
An attorney for Christa Pike said today he understood that the first thing she said upon waking up yesterday was, “Where am I and who are you?”
The attorney, Randy Spivey from the Tennessee Office of the Post-Conviction Defender, noted at a news conference after today’s hearing that he was not personally in the room when she woke up and did not want to speculate.

articles.title_orig: Tropical Storm Isaias forms in Gulf, could reach U.S. as hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.title_zh: Tropical Storm Isaias forms in Gulf, could reach U.S. as hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.content_orig:
Update: Isaias became a hurricane late Wednesday night. See the latest forecast here .
Tropical Storm Isaias was "quickly intensifying" and is expected to approach the U.S. Gulf Coast on Friday after becoming a hurricane, according to the National Hurricane Center .
Currently swirling in the Gulf, Isaias would be the Atlantic basin's first hurricane of the season and is its ninth named storm. An El Niño climate pattern continues to bring a more active season in the Pacific. The storm formed with less than two months remaining in the 2026 hurricane season , which ends Nov. 30.
Tropical Storm Isaias, which grew from Tropical Depression Nine on Wednesday and is pronounced "ees-ah-EE-ahs," is expected to pass to the north of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula on Thursday and make landfall along the northern Gulf Coast of the U.S. late Friday or early Saturday, the hurricane center said.
A hurricane warning was issued Wednesday for the northern Gulf Coast, from Ocean Springs, Mississippi, to Florida's Bay/Gulf county line, and a tropical storm warning was issued from Louisiana's Jefferson/Plaquemines Parish line to Ocean Springs, and from the Bay/Gulf county line to Florida's Aucilla River. A storm surge warning was also issued from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Yankeetown, Florida, according to the hurricane center.
Tropical storm-force winds were extending outward up to 60 miles from the storm's center on Wednesday evening. Its maximum sustained winds were 70 mph, and it was forecast to become a hurricane by Thursday morning, the hurricane center said.
A storm's maximum wind speed must rise to at least 74 mph to be considered a hurricane.
Isaias is forecast to bring moderate to heavy rainfall to the Gulf Coast and into the rest of the Southeast this weekend into early next week. The hurricane center forecasts 3 to 7 inches of rain and as much as 10 inches in some places on the central Gulf Coast from southeastern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle. Much of the Southeast, and as far north as the Tennessee Valley and the Carolinas, could see rainfall ranging from 1 to 5 inches, forecasters said.
Some longer-range forecast models also see this moisture eventually reaching the Ohio Valley and Northeast by midweek next week.
The hurricane center on Thursday warned of "an increasing risk of dangerous wind and storm surge impacts" along parts of the northern Gulf Coast and urged people living in Louisiana, Alabama, Mississippi and northern Florida to "closely monitor the latest forecast updates and ensure they have their hurricane plan in place."
At high tide, the approximately 300-mile stretch between Ocean Springs, Mississippi, and Indian Pass, Florida, could see a storm surge of up to 7 feet, forecasters said, potentially causing major flooding.
In addition to rain, the hurricane center said Isaias could potentially bring urban flooding and isolated river flooding to places in its path.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis on Tuesday signed an executive order declaring a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties ahead of the storm's arrival. DeSantis said in a statement that the order "ensures communities have the time and resources necessary to prepare for potential severe weather impacts to the Panhandle and Big Bend region of Florida."
On Wednesday, Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey issued a similar state of emergency for 40 counties, saying in a statement that it will allow Alabama officials "to take any needed steps ahead of landfall."
While tropical storm and hurricane formation and frequency vary throughout the season, the "I"-named systems tend to be the most retired names within the Atlantic basin.
The most commonly known retired "I"-named storms are Ian (2022), Ida (2021), Irma (2017) and Irene (2011).
When Ike was retired in 2008, Isaias replaced the "I" name on the Atlantic tropical cyclones list, which rotates every six years.

articles.title_orig: Japan ranked best country in the world for fourth straight year
articles.title_zh: Japan ranked best country in the world for fourth straight year
articles.content_orig:
Japan was named the world’s most attractive country for the fourth consecutive year, according to survey results released Wednesday, extending a winning streak as record numbers of overseas visitors continue to flock to the country.
Japan took the top spot in the U.S. edition of the magazine Conde Nast Traveler’s Readers’ Choice Awards for “Best Countries in the World.”
Italy ranked second, followed by Ireland, Cambodia and Spain.
The results demonstrate the country’s enduring appeal among international travelers as inbound tourism continues to surge . A record 42.7 million overseas visitors came to Japan in 2025, according to Justice Ministry figures.
Tokyo’s Haneda Airport was ranked the sixth best in the world, with Singapore’s Changi Airport taking the top place.
In a news release Wednesday, the Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) said Japan’s strong showing reflected not only the appeal of its tourism resources, but also qualities distinctive to Japan, such as its hospitality and safety.
“We hope that this continued international recognition will generate even greater interest in Japan and encourage more people to visit,” the organization wrote.
Conde Nast Traveler readers cast 798,867 votes in this year’s awards, the magazine’s 39th edition. The awards, held annually since 1988, rank destinations and travel experiences based on readers’ overall evaluations, with voting across categories including countries, hotels and cruises.
In the magazine’s U.K. edition of the rankings, Japan placed second behind Greece, with Italy, Turkey and Portugal completing the top five. The magazine highlighted the country’s restaurants, hot springs, cherry blossoms and high-speed rail network, as well as its mix of traditional culture, design and technological innovation.
“We will continue to showcase the unique attractions of regions across Japan, including their nature, culture, and cuisine, to audiences around the world, while encouraging travel to regional destinations and working toward sustainable tourism,” JNTO wrote.

articles.title_orig: Naval drone hits oil tanker off Russian resort city Sochi, triggering massive blaze
articles.title_zh: Naval drone hits oil tanker off Russian resort city Sochi, triggering massive blaze
articles.content_orig:
Russian officials said a Liberian-flagged tanker was attacked and a crew of 23 Indian nationals rescued
An oil tanker off Russia’s Black Sea coast was struck by a naval drone, triggering a huge fire and black smoke cloud that blanketed parts of the resort city of Sochi, Russia’s transport ministry has said.
The transport ministry said a Liberian-flagged tanker had been attacked and that “crude oil is burning openly in the waters of the Black Sea”.
“Firefighting efforts will begin once the fire’s intensity has subsided and rescue vessels can safely approach the tanker,” the ministry said.
A crew of 23 – all Indian citizens – had been rescued, it added.
Russia and Ukraine have targeted commercial shipping around the Black Sea since the conflict began, and Russia has recently attacked grain vessels carrying Ukrainian goods near the coast of Romania.
There was no comment from Kyiv on the attack.
Videos and photos circulated on social media from Sochi – a popular Black Sea resort city of almost 500,000 people – showed bright orange flames out at sea and a thick column of black smoke billowing into the sky.
Local officials restricted access to the coast and beaches.
Elsewhere on Tuesday, Bulgaria’s prime minister said that two commercial vessels had been struck by drones in the first attack on shipping in the Nato member’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea.
Bulgarian authorities said that the origin of the drones was under investigation, but Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy blamed Russia for the drone strikes. Bulgarian prime minister Rumen Radev condemned the attack.
After an emergency government meeting, Radev said: “This is an unacceptable attack in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone. It is a blatant violation of international law and maritime law.”
Sea and aerial drones attacked the ships about 80 miles (128km) off Bulgaria’s coast, he said.
Zelenskyy warned in his nightly address on Tuesday that a “massive strike” from Russia was likely to come, and in the early hours of Wednesday Kyiv was attacked.
Russian strikes damaged buildings and warehouses across the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv’s mayor ​Vitali ‌Klitschko said ‌on Telegram.
Agence France-Presse reported multiple explosions in Kyiv, and Reuters reported two people were killed by Russian strikes.
A separate Russian strike on Ukraine’s south-eastern city of Dnipro damaged ⁠an industrial facility, ​officials said, without giving details.
Kyiv has been under increased attack as winter approaches, with Russian airstrikes targeting energy infrastructure, rail and road transport, including bridges that connect the city over the Dnipro river. Air raid sirens have sounded almost constantly day and night, urging residents to take cover in basements, shelters and subway stations.
With Reuters and Agence France-Presse

articles.title_orig: Margaret Hamilton, Whose Software Guided the Apollo Missions, Has Died
articles.title_zh: Margaret Hamilton, Whose Software Guided the Apollo Missions, Has Died
articles.content_orig:
Margaret Hamilton, a profoundly influential computer scientist best known for leading the software engineering team at MIT’s Instrumentation Lab during NASA’s Apollo program, died on Sep. 30. She was 90.
A computing pioneer who authored over 130 publications, Hamilton helped to establish software engineering as a dedicated discipline. She worked at MIT from 1959 until the mid-1970s, after which she became a successful computing entrepreneur and CEO.
Her life’s work was recognized with many awards and honors, including the 2016 Presidential Medal of Freedom from President Barack Obama, whose citation noted: “Hamilton defined new forms of software engineering and helped launch an industry that would forever change human history. Her software architecture led to giant leaps for humankind, writing the code that helped America set foot on the moon.”
“To say Margaret Hamilton was a pioneer — to say she was ahead of her time — would be a dramatic understatement. She was a software engineer at a time when that field was in its infancy, and she not only developed advanced code herself but also led a team in using that nascent technology to develop one of the most complex systems humanity had ever achieved,” says Olivier de Weck, the Apollo Program Professor and interim head of the MIT Department Aeronautics and Astronautics.
“The Apollo program still stands as one of our greatest testaments to the power of collaboration, ingenuity, and engineering, and Margaret Hamilton was a fundamental contributor to that program’s success. And for her that was just the beginning! She went on to become an entrepreneur and remained on the cutting edge of systems software throughout an extraordinary career, while acting as an advocate, mentor, and inspiration to millions.”
Early life and projects at MIT
Born in Paoli, Indiana, in 1936, Hamilton began studying mathematics at the University of Michigan in 1955 before transferring to Earlham College, where she earned a BA in mathematics with a minor in philosophy in 1958. She moved to Boston, Massachusetts, in 1959 with her husband while he pursued a law degree.
Hamilton soon found a temporary position in the meteorology department at MIT, working with professor of meteorology Edward N. Lorenz SM ’43, ScD ’48 on weather prediction software. This was her first entry point into computer programming, and her work would go on to inform Lorenz’s future publications on chaos theory.
From there, Hamilton took a role as a programmer at MIT Lincoln Laboratory in 1961, working on the Semi-Automatic Ground Environment (SAGE) project, the United States’ first air defense system. Hamilton wrote software for the prototype AN/FSQ-7 computer (XD-1), used by the U.S. Air Force to search for potentially unfriendly aircraft. During this time, Hamilton began to take an interest in software reliability — a new and largely unexplored concept at the time.
In 1965 Hamilton was preparing to pursue graduate studies when her husband saw an advertisement in the newspaper: The Instrumentation Lab at MIT was seeking people to develop software to “send man to the moon.” The lab had won the contract from NASA to build the onboard flight software for the Apollo program. Intrigued by the challenge, Hamilton applied, and was hired as the first programmer for the Apollo project at MIT, as well as the first female programmer in the project.
Hamilton worked first on the software for the uncrewed Apollo missions and then was promoted into leading the team developing the on-board flight software for the crewed missions. By 1968 she was assistant director in charge of the Command and Service Module team, and more than 400 people were working on Apollo’s software.
“From my own perspective, the software experience itself (designing it, developing it, evolving it, watching it perform and learning from it for future systems) was at least as exciting as the events surrounding the mission,” Hamilton told MIT News in 2009 . “There was no second chance. We knew that. We took our work seriously, many of us beginning this journey while still in our 20s. Coming up with solutions and new ideas was an adventure. Dedication and commitment were a given. Mutual respect was across the board. Because software was a mystery, a black box, upper management gave us total freedom and trust. We had to find a way, and we did. Looking back, we were the luckiest people in the world; there was no choice but to be pioneers.”
“Defensive” programming and priority-driven software take humans to the moon
Hamilton discovered a talent for leadership, as well as a keen instinct for problem-solving and critical thinking that would prove to save Project Apollo several times over.
There was the incident that became known as “the Lauren error”: One day, her daughter Lauren, then four years old, was playing with the command module simulator at the Instrumentation Lab when she somehow activated a pre-launch program, called P01, while the simulator was in midflight — which crashed the simulator altogether. Hamilton created a program add-on in the technical documentation warning users not to launch P01 during flight.
She also proposed a software fix to prevent the error happening during a real mission, but she was overruled on the grounds that the highly trained astronauts were never going to make that same mistake. Yet during the Apollo 8 mission in 1968, that’s exactly what happened: Jim Lovell inadvertently launched P01 during the flight, causing the on-flight navigational data to vanish. Hamilton and her team were called in to solve the error, and after that her proposed changes were integrated into the program. This was an early example of “defensive” programming, the practice of building software that could anticipate or fix errors on its own.
Hamilton’s most famous contribution to the Apollo program came during the pivotal Apollo 11 mission to land on the moon in July of 1969. Moments before the Eagle module was set to land on the lunar surface, the onboard computer raised the alarm. It had detected a 1202 error: The computer was overloaded due to a fault in a hardware switch, and it was possible the system would not be able to handle the complex landing procedure.
But Hamilton and her team had engineered priority-driven software, able to shut down unnecessary background tasks in order to prioritize mission-critical tasks. Houston trusted Hamilton’s software and allowed the mission to proceed, and two men walked on the moon for the first time.
Hamilton continued to work at the Instrumentation Lab into the 1970s. As the Apollo program wound down, the Instrumentation Lab spun out of MIT to become the independent Draper Laboratory .
“Margaret left an indelible mark on Draper, and we will be forever grateful,” says Jerry M. Wohletz SM ’97, PhD ’00, president and CEO at Draper. “Through her leadership and contributions to the development of the onboard flight software for NASA’s Apollo Guidance Computer, she helped ensure that Apollo astronauts landed safely on the lunar surface and safely returned home. We will honor her legacy at Draper forever.”
Hamilton went on to create her first software company, Higher Order Software, in 1976. The firm was based on Hamilton’s software engineering approach of error prevention and fault tolerance.
A decade later, Hamilton founded another software company, Hamilton Technologies, “to provide products and services to modernize the planning, system engineering and software development process in order to maximize reliability, lower cost and accelerate time to market.”
Hamilton Technologies’ flagship product is the Universal Systems Language (USL), a systems modeling language and methodology for engineering complex software systems that prioritize error prevention and defensive programming.
Throughout her career, Hamilton worked to achieve recognition for software engineering as a dedicated discipline.

articles.title_orig: ByteDance heads first SCMP Plus Going Global 100 ranking
articles.title_zh: ByteDance heads first SCMP Plus Going Global 100 ranking
articles.content_orig:
Social media giant beats out Foxconn Industrial, Shein and BYD in new SCMP Plus ranking of China’s global champions
TikTok owner ByteDance is China’s Going Global champion, according to a new SCMP Plus databank tracking mainland companies’ overseas expansion efforts.
About two-thirds of the Going Global 100 members are technology or consumer companies, such as carmakers, reflecting how private businesses are driving China’s overseas growth through the development of cutting-edge technology and the creation of their own global brands. Private manufacturers are also now outpacing state-owned enterprises (SOEs) in overseas expansion, as they move beyond being assemblers for multinational brands and look to escape cutthroat price wars at home.
“Private firms have started to dominate, given the growing prominence of consumer electronics, e-commerce platforms, digital tech, EVs and green tech and even light manufacturing,” said Jayant Menon, senior fellow at the ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute in Singapore.

articles.title_orig: As China and the EU begin crunch trade talks, optimism is in short supply
articles.title_zh: As China and the EU begin crunch trade talks, optimism is in short supply
articles.content_orig:
Observers on both sides are braced for more turbulence – and mainly hope Beijing and Brussels can avoid a full-blown trade conflict
As China and the European Union began a fresh round of trade talks in Beijing on Thursday, observers on both sides appeared to agree on one thing: a big breakthrough was unlikely.
Chinese firms based in Europe said they hoped the talks could achieve some “limited progress” to help stabilise the trade relationship, while European analysts remained cautious about the potential outcome.
“They’re bound to get some results,” said a Chinese source with knowledge of the talks, adding that EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic “will not go home empty-handed”.
The China Chamber of Commerce to the EU called on both sides to make full use of the Trade and Investment Consultations (TIC) mechanism to manage differences, push for solutions and send clearer signals to businesses.

articles.title_orig: Accused Chinese spy’s crypto cash flow, ‘unfit mother’ claims exposed in court
articles.title_zh: Accused Chinese spy’s crypto cash flow, ‘unfit mother’ claims exposed in court
articles.content_orig:
The Southern California real estate agent accused of spying on a prominent Taiwanese family for China allegedly had access to $190,000 in a secret Chinese crypto account, as allegations surfaced that the she is “an unfit mother” at a court hearing Wednesday.
Wanying Zhang appeared in an LA courthouse wearing a white jumpsuit and shackles alongside new attorney Craig Harbaugh, who asked for home confinement for his client. The government vehemently argued that she was a flight risk.
At the hearing, prosecutors accused Zhang of having access to $190,000 in a secret Chinese cryptocurrency account that she “was still receiving profits from.” They also pointed to Zhang’s brother having ties to the Chinese government.
Prosecutors referenced a seized iCloud video they said would show Zhang was “a danger to society,” arguing that her ties to “her family may not be as strong as they seem” as her husband Edric Ding looked on.
“You should have produced this video and I could say she’s an unfit mother,” Judge Steve Kim said, as it was revealed that Zhang has “young children.”
Prosecutors also pointed to a dozen one-way trips Zhang allegedly took to China, Paris and Japan. Harbaugh argued that purchasing one-way tickets was more economical.
Judge Kim ruled Zhang was a flight risk, and she was taken into custody by US Marshals without bail.
She’s expected back in court on October 19.
Zhang’s initial hearing on Monday took a bizarre turn when her public defender, Chad Pennington, asked for a side conversation with the judge seconds after the proceeding began, leading to a lengthy 20-minute court recess.
When the parties returned, Zhang was asked if she understood what she was accused of and answered “yes.”
The real estate agent was arrested at LAX Sunday after being accused of spying for China. Zhang, also known as “Heather,” was busted as she tried to board a flight to Shanghai.
Video taken shortly after the arrest showed several FBI agents leading the handcuffed Zhang through an airport terminal.
The 34-year-old, who lives in Irvine, is accused of working with handlers from the People’s Republic of China to surveil the son of Taiwan President Ching-te Lai.
Zhang, who worked for a real estate firm along with her husband, allegedly traveled to Seattle in September 2025 to spy on Ting-Yu Lai, an engineer in his 30s who is based in the US.
Surveillance camera photographs also allegedly caught Zhang sitting in a car with an accomplice taking pictures of his house and close relatives.
She appeared to have lived a jet-setting lifestyle before federal authorities detained her.
Zhang documented trips to Paris and outings with friends across the West Coast on her social media pages.
She also appeared to have graduated from USC, where the total cost of attendance can run more than $75,000 per year.
Ding’s social media shows outings to Korean barbecue restaurants, as well as anime and sword-art expos.
The couple is also seen posing with what appears to be their child.
Zhang’s arrest comes amid several other high-profile California cases involving allegations of covert Chinese government activity or influence.
Disgraced former Arcadia mayor Eileen Wang entered a plea in federal court following the bombshell admission she was a spy for China in March.
Former Democratic Rep. Eric Swalwell confessed to a prescription drug-fueled sex romp with a suspected Chinese spy Christine Fang, also known as “Fang Fang,” according to newly released FBI files in August.
“We have a problem with Beijing using Chinese Americans for their own purposes in California,” First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said. “They are using them for their own foreign affairs because they are playing the long game to get a competitive advantage over us.”

articles.title_orig: Donald Trump’s Texas rally rocked by repeated protests
articles.title_zh: Donald Trump’s Texas rally rocked by repeated protests
articles.content_orig:
Trump briefly stepped away from the microphone after one protester appeared to approach the stage
Donald Trump’s latest campaign rally was rocked by repeated protests on Wednesday as the US president urged Texas voters to back embattled Senate candidate Ken Paxton.
At least half a dozen demonstrators interrupted the US president during his remarks in San Antonio, with some led away by police. One was physically assaulted by an older Trump supporter as he tried to leave the arena.
Trump briefly stepped away from the microphone after one protester appeared to approach the stage. “He’s going back home to mom,” the president said after the man was removed. “But what he doesn’t know is his mom voted for Trump.”
Supporters waving cowboy hats and chanting “USA” drowned out some of the protesters, while Trump told demonstrators to “get the hell out of here”. He mocked their appearance and claimed without evidence that “they’re paid by enemies of our nation”.
The president also used Wednesday’s rally to address recent comments in which he appeared to suggest that Iran could destroy Los Angeles or San Diego, earning widespread condemnation from Democrats.
In remarks that were again less than crystal clear, Trump said: “I said it the other day, let them hit a missile into San Diego or Los Angeles on the way. Let them hit – you want to see a horror show? You want to see problems? Let them hit San Diego. Let them hit Los Angeles and you want to see some bad things happen.
“You want to see a country that would be in freefall. We’re not going to let that happen. We protect our cities, we protect our country, we’re not letting that happen. And they’d use it, too. They’d use it.”
Trump was making his third trip to Texas in less than a month as Republicans pour money into races they had expected to win comfortably in November’s midterm elections.
Paxton, whom Trump endorsed during the Republican primary after turning against the incumbent senator John Cornyn, was called on stage by the president and thanked him for his support.
“Mr President, I want to thank you for coming for me, for coming for us, and for coming for Texas,” Paxton said. “We are going to win this race.”
Trump described Paxton as “perhaps the greatest attorney general in the United States of America,” and said: “He was tough and he was with us all the way. He’s a fantastic man.”
The Republican campaign to maintain control of the Senate has become increasingly focused on Texas, where Democrat James Talarico has emerged as a serious threat. A New York Times/ Siena College poll released last weekend showed Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 45% among likely voters. Texas has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988.
Trump won the state by almost 14 percentage points in 2024, but his approval rating has fallen sharply. A Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday put his approval rating at 32%, while registered voters preferred Democrats to Republicans 44%-37%.
Trump’s relationship with Paxton has sometimes appeared uneasy. Trump called Paxton “a pain in the ass sometimes” last week, but on Wednesday did not discuss a leaked recording of Paxton in which the Senate candidate reportedly complained about the war in Iran, rising fuel prices and the way his campaign was being run.
Instead he spent much of the rally attacking Talarico, whom he repeatedly referred to as “Tala-freako”. He claimed without evidence that Talarico is vegan and recently disappeared: “He’s sick because he’s been forced to eat meat for political reasons and he’s throwing up all over the place.”
Trump insisted: “The people of Texas are not going to let weak, gutless, self-hating, transgender-promoting freak shows destroy everything that we’ve built.”
The president’s political difficulties in Texas were underlined by the absence of Republican governor Greg Abbott, a close Trump ally who is himself facing a competitive re-election race against Democratic state representative Gina Hinojosa.
Abbott was instead due to attend the dedication of a hospital about 330 miles away. Democrats seized on his decision not to appear with Trump.
Republicans have now devoted more than $300m to elections in Texas, according to the Associated Press, while Trump’s broader 32-day campaign blitz has taken him through several Republican-leaning states, including Oklahoma, Alabama, Ohio and Nebraska.

articles.title_orig: Coco Gauff explained how online harassment "drained" her in China Open
articles.title_zh: Coco Gauff explained how online harassment "drained" her in China Open
articles.content_orig:
By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER
Published: 06:30 EDT, 7 October 2026 | Updated: 10:09 EDT, 7 October 2026
Coco Gauff was knocked out of China Open amid concerns over her health one day after the American star highlighted the vile racism she had encountered after being mixed up in a 'cheating' storm against 16-year-old Sun Xinran.
The two-time Grand Slam champion had been 5-4 down in her third-round tie in Beijing when she patted a straightforward volley over the net, which Sun charged up the court to send back for a winner.
But Gauff had thrown up her arms in complaint as the forehand sailed over her head, telling the chair umpire that she had been distracted by a sponsor change on the electronic advertising boards on both sides of the court.
With the point replayed, Gauff wrenched momentum from her opponent and booked her spot in the fourth round - only to struggle from the early stages against world No19 Elise Mertens.
Level on serve at 4-3, Gauff's game unravelled to lose the next six games, with the US star telling her camp with some concern at 4-1 in the second set that she didn't know why she was so low on fighting spirit.
'I have no energy. I'm trying, I have no energy. I can't see the ball, I feel like I'm going to pass out,' she told the team in her player's box. 'I'm going to just try to finish the match.'
Coco Gauff sparked health concerns after revealing she was going to 'pass out' during her defeat by Elise Mertens in China
In the build-up to the match the US star had to contend with vile racism on social media after she requested a replayed point in her third-round match against Sun Xinran
Gauff eventually lost 6-3, 6-3, downed in straight sets for the first time since February.
After the match, Gauff admitted that the events of the previous day had taken their toll.
'It has been kind of draining, I'm not going to lie,' she said. 'I just turn off my phone and move on. There's nothing you can do.
'I think today I was just a bit flat. I just didn't play well. I think I wasn't moving well. There were a lot of things I didn't do well.'
The 22-year-old's preparations were marred in the build-up as she struggled in the face of racist abuse on social media in the wake of her controversial point against Sun.
Sharing a statement to clarify when she had stopped the match as she had done, Gauff sought to set the record straight after being accused that she had only protested due to her low-quality volley.
Gauff cited a flicker at the beginning of the point which she admitted she wasn't sure 'if that is what I actually saw'.
Continuing, the former US Open champion wrote: 'We are told before the matches we are allowed to continue to finish play so KEEP IT [in] MIND I am thinking about all this while I'm playing the point.
'Anything can be challenged after the point is over (as in most sports you can review a call after the play is over, I personally think this is the correct rule). If I would've lost the point my opponent is also free to do the same thing and ask for a replay and she would've been completely in her right to do so.
'When it flickered again I raised my hands before she hit her shot because this is when I was sure I saw the light flicker and it wasn't my mind doing tricks lol (which again doesn't matter because anything can be challenged after the point).
'It was an unfortunate situation but it is out of my control, the think pieces and calling me unfair is ridiculous when those are the rules. I did not make them, I think it's weird I'm getting hate for following the rules.
Gauff told reporters of the toll the cheating storm had taken on her after her defeat
'Xinran is [an] incredible talent and player, I apologized for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood. I did not like to see her so emotional as I've been there and I really understand what it is like but this is just the beginning of an incredible career.
'It was an honor to share the court in front of her home crowd.'
She also highlighted the level of racism she is subject to on social media, with her reply coming to a commenter who had written 'f*** you' to her and called her the n-word.
'Hey everyone,' Gauff replied, amplifying the comment. 'You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist.
'The amount of racist comments/dms I've received in the last few hours is insane. Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief.'
Gauff received an outpouring of support from fans in the wake of the racist abuse on social media, which was later limited after violating X's rules against hateful conduct.

articles.title_orig: Bringing local models and sandboxed tools to Windows and GitHub Copilot
articles.title_zh: Bringing local models and sandboxed tools to Windows and GitHub Copilot
articles.content_orig:
Coming soon, GitHub Copilot will determine when a task is best handled by on-device intelligence and when it should leverage cloud-scale models.
When leveraging agents, developers need both choice and control. They need technologies that offer clear boundaries for their agents and make it easy to choose the model with the right speed, performance, and cost profile for each task. That’s why GitHub offers frontier models from major model providers, as well as options like Project HydraFusion , an orchestrator choosing one or multiple models for each task while balancing performance, cost, and latency. It’s also why Windows has developed Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) to help secure interactive and non-interactive agentic coding sessions.
Coming by the end of the month, GitHub Copilot will determine when a task is best handled by on-device intelligence and when it should leverage cloud-scale models. Rather than forcing developers to manage infrastructure decisions themselves, GitHub Copilot automatically coordinates local and cloud inference behind the scenes. For NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows PCs like Surface Laptop Ultra, that means we are enabling local coding in GitHub Copilot with powerful local inference models and hardware capable of delivering a great experience at the edge.
The result is poised to be the next step in the HydraFusion vision: intelligent orchestration that spans not just multiple models, but multiple compute environments including the edge. GitHub Copilot can run commands in these environments with controlled access to files, networks, system capabilities, and credentials. Developers can automate with confidence and security in mind.
Local inference starts with a memory budget. Surface Laptop Ultra is built around NVIDIA RTX Spark, with up to 128 GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of AI compute.
With a discrete GPU, dedicated video memory is an important constraint: moving model data between system memory and the GPU can add overhead. Unified memory gives the CPU and GPU access to a shared physical pool. That makes more capacity available to the workload, but it doesn’t make all of it available to model weights.
The operating system, your applications, and the inference runtime need memory, too. So does the key-value cache, which stores attention state for tokens the model has already processed. As an agent reads files and receives tool results, its context can grow, increasing memory use and the work needed to process the next request.
Keeping a model loaded between requests can avoid repeated loading work. However, it doesn’t guarantee constant response time; context length, memory pressure, and the rest of the workload still matter. That’s why the useful question isn’t just whether a model fits, but how it behaves over a complete coding task.
To bring this local-development experience to life, Microsoft AI developed a local version of MAI Code 1.1 Flash, a coding-optimized mixture-of-experts model with 137 billion total and 6.8 billion active parameters. The on-device work applies quantization and speculative decoding to reduce the model footprint and improve end-to-end responsiveness while preserving the task completion and tool-use quality that matter in an agent loop.
Quantization reduces the precision used to represent model weights and activations, lowering memory requirements. Because code doesn’t degrade gracefully, the release evaluation must measure coding-task success as well as footprint: a single incorrect token can produce a syntax error, wrong identifier, malformed tool call, or broken diff.
Speculative decoding trades additional working memory for higher decode throughput and lower end-to-end latency. A drafter proposes candidate token blocks and the target model verifies them.
For a coding agent, the important tradeoff is whether the smaller model can still complete the same tasks. A smaller footprint is useful only if changes in code quality and tool use are understood.
With our first shipping version of MAI Code 1.1 Flash on Surface Laptop Ultra we achieve the following performance at different context lengths, with peak memory usage of 75.5GB at 256k context. At 64k and 128k context, prompt-processing throughput reaches 923.5 and 769.8 tokens per second, respectively.
The quantized version of MAI Code 1.1 Flash we use on device retains capability impressively compared to the Bfloat16 cloud variant, coming in at 53GB, an 80% reduction in size.
GitHub Copilot is adding two ways to use local models across the GitHub Copilot CLI, Copilot app, and VS Code. Developers can let Copilot’s intelligent Auto orchestration choose when to use local or cloud inference, or they can explicitly select a local model for workflows that require direct control.
With Auto, developers do not need to decide where each task should be run. Across a multi-turn session, Copilot can consider task context and cache state as it routes work between local and cloud models, preserving useful, cached work as the session evolves.
This orchestrated experience complements direct model selection, giving developers a choice between letting Copilot optimize model placement and choosing a specific local model themselves.
Explicit local-model selection supports workflows that need a specific provider, model, or endpoint. Developers can select MAI Code 1.1 Flash through the Windows ML provider or connect GitHub Copilot to OpenAI-compatible local endpoints and choose from the models those endpoints expose.
An agent’s shell commands normally inherit the access of the account running them. Moving inference onto the device doesn’t change that. Sandboxing applies a policy to the processes and local services the agent launches, controlling access to files, networks, credentials, system capabilities, and execution paths regardless of which model requested the work.
GitHub Copilot uses Microsoft Execution Containers , or MXC, an open-source library from the Windows team that translates policy into native operating-system controls. On Windows, GitHub Copilot uses the BaseContainer tier of the ProcessContainer backend. On macOS, it uses Seatbelt. On Linux, it uses bubblewrap . These local backends don’t require a separate virtual machine or container image, but we plan to make them options available through MXC in the future.
When sandboxing is enabled, shell commands and, by default, local Model Context Protocol servers and language servers run inside the process boundary. Built-in file tools run inside GitHub Copilot itself: the agent harness checks their requests against the effective policy, but those checks aren’t OS-enforced child-process isolation. Remote MCP servers are also outside the local process sandbox; when MCP sandbox controls apply, GitHub Copilot checks their connection policy in process.
Opening the GitHub Copilot CLI and running `/sandbox` slash command allows you to configure your settings at any time.
To show how these technologies work together, let’s use a real-world example.
Consider a job that reads local repositories, runs their tests in working copies, and writes one HTML report each morning. The source repositories should remain read-only, and the test processes shouldn’t access the network. Model selection is independent: the same job can use a configured local or cloud model.
Open the settings dialog by clicking the gear icon in the GitHub Copilot app and selecting your project in the left menu. For this example, we’ll be using the `copilot-sdk` repo that hosts our opensource GitHub Copilot Runtime/SDK project.
Enabling the `Sandbox new sessions` toggle turns on sandboxing by default whenever you work within that project. By default, it’s current working directly is read/write while the rest of the system remains largely read-only or inaccessible to an agent.
Select the` Automations` section on the left navigation and click the `Start automation` button to open the dialog that allows you to configure a new automation.
Aft

articles.title_orig: World Health Organization says Russian lab worker’s death has not been clearly linked to plague
articles.title_zh: World Health Organization says Russian lab worker’s death has not been clearly linked to plague
articles.content_orig:
Frank McGeorge, MD , Local 4's Medical Expert
The World Health Organization says Russian authorities have reported no plague cases in the Irkutsk region.
The worker’s cause of death remains unclear.
A worker at a Siberian research institute that studies plague died after developing pneumonia, prompting officials to monitor and quarantine people who had contact with her and renewing questions about a disease many associate with the Middle Ages.
But Russian authorities have reported no plague cases in the region.
The World Health Organization said Russian officials described the worker’s illness as initially resembling a typical acute respiratory viral infection.
Officials have not publicly established the cause of death.
The worker died Oct. 2 at a hospital near Irkutsk, according to Reuters.
About 200 people who had contact with her were quarantined, and a local official said 60% had since been released.
Russian officials said no plague was found among the contacts who had been tested.
The WHO said it has been in contact with Russian authorities. Reports of the death have fueled speculation online, but Reuters reported there is no public evidence supporting the theories circulating on social media.
The incident has also revived memories of COVID-19.
But plague is not a new or unidentified disease. COVID-19 was caused by a newly identified virus; plague is caused by Yersinia pestis, a well-studied bacterium that persists in animal populations in parts of Africa, Asia and the Americas.
Dr. Leonard Johnson said plague persists in animal populations and continues to cause sporadic human cases around the world, including in the United States.
The CDC has said there is no indication of a broader threat to the United States from the Russian case.
There are three main forms of plague.
Bubonic plague, the most common, typically follows the bite of an infected flea and causes swollen lymph nodes.
Septicemic plague affects the blood; both it and bubonic plague are generally acquired through infected fleas.
Pneumonic plague affects the lungs and can spread through respiratory droplets from an infected person or animal, usually with close contact.
Pneumonic plague can be highly fatal if untreated, said Dr. Leonard Johnson, chief of infectious diseases at Henry Ford St. John Hospital.
But modern antibiotics can treat plague when given promptly. Johnson said people identified as close contacts of a confirmed case could be given preventive antibiotics, including doxycycline or ciprofloxacin, to reduce the chance of secondary infections.
He said the risk of wider spread remains low, particularly in the United States. That is a sharp contrast with the medieval epidemics that killed millions.
Experts remain cautious because they do not have direct access to the underlying information, and public statements by Russian authorities have not clearly established the cause of death.
So far, however, reports do not confirm plague or indicate a wider outbreak.

Dr. McGeorge can be seen on Local 4 News helping Metro Detroiters with health concerns when he isn't helping save lives in the emergency room at Henry Ford Hospital.

articles.title_orig: AEW Grand Slam: France Dynamite Results – Will Ospreay Keeps AEW World Title from Okada, Mercedes Moné Retains AEW Women’s World Title vs. Queen Aminata, More
articles.title_zh: AEW Grand Slam: France Dynamite Results – Will Ospreay Keeps AEW World Title from Okada, Mercedes Moné Retains AEW Women’s World Title vs. Queen Aminata, More
articles.content_orig:
AEW's debut in Paris was a special one, as Grand Slam: France Dynamite emanated from Adidas Arena on TBS and HBO Max! A major debut called for a huge card, and Paris responded with energy that could be felt from the opening bell and beyond the main event! As if the excitement wasn’t high enough, we’re just 11 days from AEW WrestleDream in Orlando!
In the main event, AEW World Champion Will Ospreay defeated AEW International Champion “The Rainmaker” Kazuchika Okada to retain his title in an unbelievable match, which marked the first time Ospreay beat Okada in a championship bout. As Ospreay celebrated in the ring with “Speedball” Mike Bailey, Samoa Joe appeared on the ramp to end the night, sending a message that he’s ready for Clockwork Carnage after qualifying by beating “Jungle” Jack Perry earlier in the night.
AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné got everything she could handle from Queen Aminata in front of a Parisian crowd that was fully behind Aminata’s quest to win her first AEW gold. Moné overcame Aminata in the end to get the win, but she could not celebrate for long because her WrestleDream opponent, Thekla, hit the ring to cut Moné in half with a spear!
The night began with ROH World Champion Bandido turning away AEW World Trios Champion Kofi while both men’s trios partners made their presence felt, specifically Swerve Strickland and “Hangman” Adam Page. Later, Swerve and The New Level challenged Page, Bandido and Brody King to face them in a 2-out-of-3 falls match for the AEW World Trios Championship at WrestleDream!
TNT Champion Darby Allin was left a bloody mess in his defense against former champion “The Protostar” Kyle Fletcher, but somehow Allin was able to leave Paris with a successful defense in a brutally violent encounter.  Plus, Mark Davis and Jake Doyle earned a huge win for the Don Callis Family in tag team action over Gabe Kidd and AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley!
All that and more went down on our first night in Paris!
The night began with the ROH World Championship on the line! Kofi, one third of the AEW World Trios Champions, made his way to the ring to a raucous ovation inside the Adidas Arena, accompanied by another third of the champions, Austin Creed.
The champion came out next, and he wasn't alone either — Bandido was flanked by Brody King for this championship tilt.
The referee called for the Code of Honor, and not only did both men shake hands, but they embraced. A hyped-up crowd was fully behind this matchup, which only fed the energy of both Kofi and Bandido.
While both men brought a clear level of speed, there was an extended feeling-out process to start, with each grabbing a brief advantage before the action reset to a stalemate. After both went for dropkicks, Bandido popped right back to his feet, but Kofi came back with a second dropkick that sent Bandido to the floor. When Kofi tried to dive to the outside, Bandido simply stepped out of the way, and Kofi's head bounced off the top rope. Bandido tried to climb back to the apron, but Kofi caught him with another dropkick, knocking him to the floor again. Kofi then charged and flipped over the top rope onto the floor, crushing Bandido, and took control of the early going.
Kofi rolled Bandido back into the ring and climbed the ropes. As Bandido got to his feet, Kofi leaped off the top for a cross body — but Bandido caught him in mid-air and, in an incredible display of strength, lifted him into a delayed vertical suplex, holding him aloft one-armed as the crowd counted all the way to twenty before finally dropping him to the mat.
The sheer exhaustion of that suplex left both men down. It was then that Swerve Strickland, the third member of the AEW World Trios Champions, made his way out with Prince Nana to join Creed in supporting Kofi. Only steps behind him, however, was “Hangman” Adam Page, and when Swerve spotted him, Creed and Nana had to hold him back. Page simply walked past and joined King at ringside to support their partner.
Bandido played to the crowd before turning his attention back to Kofi, landing a pair of corner strikes followed by a diving gut check that doubled Kofi over in pain. Bandido fired off more strikes in an adjacent corner, but when he went for a third, Kofi slipped away and whipped him to the opposite corner. With Bandido seated against the turnbuckle, Kofi drove a running knee into the side of his face, followed by elevated stomps to the chest. Kofi then ran in from the opposite corner for a shotgun dropkick, connecting flush. He covered, but Bandido kicked out to keep his title reign alive.
A visibly frustrated Kofi took a moment to regroup before pulling Bandido up, hitting a headbutt and an uppercut to back him into the corner and hoist him up top for a superplex attempt. But when Kofi came up after him, Bandido turned it around with a gorilla press slam, dumping Kofi onto the top turnbuckle before following with a dropkick that put him on the mat! Bandido covered, but Kofi kicked out at two.
Bandido tried to whip Kofi across the ring, but Kofi reversed it with a kick to the stomach, then leaped for a leg drop to the back of Bandido's head. Kofi started building momentum, landing backhanded chops followed by a jumping side kick that put Bandido back down. Bandido avoided a follow-up jumping clothesline and whipped Kofi to the corner, but as he rushed in, Kofi flipped back with a pendulum kick through the ropes, then went up top for a frog splash cross body that got another near-fall.
Kofi bounced off the ropes for a jumping lariat, then fired up the Paris crowd before connecting with a Boom Drop. As Bandido stumbled to his feet, Kofi measured him for T.I.P., but Bandido ducked out of the way. Kofi spun him around in a rear waistlock and sent him to the corner. Bandido kicked his way out and leaped to the top rope for a reverse tornillo that got a two-count.
Bandido pushed Kofi into the ropes, but Kofi rebounded with a jumping spin kick to the head for another near-fall. The crowd roared as Bandido started to fight back, only for Kofi to cut him off with a kick to the gut. The two traded strikes off the ropes until Bandido popped Kofi up into a knee strike. As Bandido came off the ropes, Kofi leaped into the air and stomped him into the mat.
The crowd was fully invested as both men's partners continued to will them on from ringside. Bandido rose in the corner as Kofi waited in the opposite one; when Kofi charged in, Bandido met him with a kick combination and climbed to the second rope. As Bandido came off, Kofi caught him and rolled him through for an SOS into the second buckle! That’s a new and brutal variation on that move, matching Bandido's own escalating viciousness in this battle for championship gold.
As Creed and Swerve, along with the crowd, urged Kofi toward the top rope, he slowly made his way up. With Bandido doubled over below, Kofi leaped off and splashed him flat onto his back! That was an unorthodox execution, but even more devastating!  Bandido kicked out to preserve his reign!
Kofi dug deeper into his arsenal than ever before, fully aware of the caliber of champion standing across from him. He made his way back to the top rope, but with Creed's back turned to hype the crowd, nobody saw Bandido sneak up from behind to catch Kofi with a kick. Bandido joined him on the top rope, and with both men balanced precariously, Bandido grabbed Kofi and hit a Revolutionary Fly from the top! He covered, 1-2-Kofi got a hand on the bottom rope to stay alive! Bandido picked up Kofi for the X-Knee, but Kofi landed on his feet and hit an SOS for a near-fall!
An argument broke out between Hangman and Swerve at ringside, and the two got in a shoving match, with both men having to be separated from each other. In the ensuing commotion, Bandido pulled Kofi off the mat with the 21 Plex for the three-count. As Bandido celebrated, Page and Swerve still had to be separated, with King telling Page that all that matters is that Band
